name: Lexical Sophistication
description: Measures word frequency bands and lexical sophistication to identify AI text's tendency toward common, high-frequency vocabulary.
useCase: Detecting AI text through systematic preference for common words and avoidance of rare terms
mechanism: Maps each content word to its frequency rank in reference corpora (e.g., SUBTLEX, BNC) and computes the proportion of words in different frequency bands (high/mid/low frequency). Also calculates lexical sophistication indices using Academic Word List coverage and word concreteness ratings. AI text typically shows a bias toward mid-frequency 'safe' vocabulary, avoiding both very common colloquialisms and rare specialized terms.
source: Kyle, K. & Crossley, S. A. (2015) - Automatically Assessing Lexical Sophistication, Journal of Applied Linguistics
algorithm: Frequency Band Analysis + AWL Coverage + Concreteness Rating + Statistical Profiling
parameters: Corpus: SUBTLEX-US/BNC, Bands: 1k/2k/5k/10k/off-list, AWL levels: 1-10, Concreteness: Brysbaert norms, Min text: 100 words
strengths:
• Well-validated psycholinguistic foundations
• Captures vocabulary sophistication patterns
• Multiple complementary sub-metrics
• Language-independent framework
limitations:
• Domain-specific text confounds frequency-based measures
• Technical text naturally uses off-list words
• LLMs can be prompted for specific vocabulary levels
• Requires robust frequency data per language

references.title: Kyle, K. & Crossley, S. A. (2015). Automatically Assessing Lexical Sophistication: Indices, Tools, Findings, and Application. TESOL Quarterly.
Kobak, D. et al. (2024). Delving into ChatGPT Usage in Academic Writing Through Excess Vocabulary. arXiv.
Brysbaert, M. et al. (2014). Concreteness Ratings for 40 Thousand Generally Known English Word Lemmas. Behavior Research Methods.
